author: Declaration Desk
title: Gukesh springs a rare Berlin line but Sindarov holds; match level at 1.5-1.5 after Game 3
dek: The champion pressed for most of a 60-move game with Black before it ended in an opposite-coloured bishop endgame. Gukesh has White in Game 4 on Saturday after a rest day.
body:
D. Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov drew Game 3 of the World Chess Championship in Geneva on Thursday after 60 moves, the third draw in three games, leaving the 14-game match level at 1.5-1.5.

With Black, Gukesh sprang a surprise in the Berlin Defence, choosing 5...Be7, the Rio de Janeiro line, and then the rare 8...Nf5, a variation mostly seen in the 1980s and 1990s, instead of the usual moves. The reversal of the first two games was striking: this time it was Sindarov who left his preparation early and spent long periods thinking, while Gukesh moved quickly. The champion pressed on the kingside with ...h5 and ...g5 and later created a passed pawn on d3, but Sindarov kept the position balanced, and the game ended in an opposite-coloured bishop endgame that could not be won, according to reports.

In Games 1 and 2, Gukesh had fallen behind on the clock. Neither player has yet won a game in the match, which needs 7.5 points to win.

Friday is a rest day. Game 4 begins on Saturday at 7.30 pm IST, with Gukesh playing White.
